newsitem.title: UK: Grain charterers lift interest in Panamaxes.
newsitem.headline: Grain charterers lift interest in Panamaxes.

text.p: Brokers reported solid demand for Panamaxes and handies from grain charterers in the U.S. Gulf and also fair demand from the continent.
South America remained depressed but there were a few encouraging signs for Capers from this area as well as in the Pacific.
The BFI maintained its recent trend of appreciating between five and 10 points every day since October 2 by adding a further seven points to 1076.
But in the meantime bunker prices continue to rise steeply -- up from about $115 per tonne a week ago to $133 for fuel oil oon Tuesday, basis Rotterdam and from about $180 to $213 for diesel oil.

There is also little evidence of any revival in the prices of vessels sold for scrap -- a 20,000 dwt bulker for example consigned to India for demolition currently could expect to fetch about $165 per lightweight tonne against over $200 a couple of months ago.
GRAIN --
On a quiet day for the number of grain fixtures reported, brokers believed rates were likely to go firmer in the North Atlantic, especially in the U.S. Gulf where the supply of handies is drying up.

Continental were said to be trading an early hss stem for U.S. Gulf/Algeria at $18.00 against $19.00 basis 34' swad and also quoted a fresh order of 20,000/10 Mississippi/Casablanca for October 24/31.
Garnac was understood to have fixed 21,500 tonnes hss U.S. Gulf/Venezuela for loading next week at $12.00 or a shade more and was open to repeat the business.
The content was also encouraging for owners with new handy wheat orders quoted today by Glencore Tilbury/Umm Qasr and Spanish Med/Libya and by Dreyfus north France/Italy.

There were reports from brokers of November orders being introduced quietly "off-market" and some early vessels on the Continent and in the west Med, such as Rena 64,129 dwt, Samson 61,345 dwt and Star of Maria 55,012 dwt, are understood to have been fixed.
Other vessels which had been at anchor awaiting events, mostly older types, were said to be preparing to trade transatlantic again.
Rumours that Halla fixed Vesta Island 69,000 dwt U.S. Gulf/Taiwan could not be verified but Nostos T 61,839 dwt was linked with NNC for a grain trip from north France to Egypt at $8,000 daily.
Toepfer quoted a new order of 70,000/10 St Lawrence/ARA and MSK 52,000 hss U.S. Gulf/Japan for Nov 10/15.

Although Cargill has another Panamax enquiry Plate and Brazil/Continent for end October and Continental today quoted for this size up River only/China for Nov 1/15 east coast South America was generally reckoned still to be a weak market for grain business in all sizes.

In the east firm rates for Panamaxes remain obtainable although details are awaited of the fixture of Amorgos 65,105 dwt for a Nopac round (possibly to Korea Line). Polydefkis P 22,235 dwt was fixed by Showa delivery Nopac trip Japan with grain on private terms.
MINERALS --

Some Caper rates have improved slightly (an unusual event in recent months). World Nord 150,000 dwt, for example, which last week was willing to fix a Pacific round at $8,500 daily has been booked by Navix prompt Japan for a Roberts Bank round at $9,500 daily.
Carbunesti has been fixed by Rohstoffhandel for 150,000 iron ore PDM/Rotterdam at close to $4.65 compared to last done of $4.55.

Not very significant improvements, but brokers also report a good volume of fresh enquiry today for November Capers - Navix delivery West Australia via Dunkirk redelivery Far East, Hanjin Cape Lambert to the Continent, AK Bridge NSW/Ensted and BHP Queensland/Constanza.

Rumoured fixtures include Stellar ERA 149,321 dwt to Cetragpa for Bolivar/Hadera, World Action 150,790 dwt to Nippon Steel for West Australia/Japan and Anangel Ambition 161,000 dwt to Margem for Roberts Bank/Iskenderun, but further details are lacking.
Navix are reported to have fixed a newbuilding Panamax ex yard Japan this month at $9,500 daily for 12 months.
